bugs.name: Create Tag Only reports an existing release when retrying an already-created standalone tag
bugs.summary: Retrying Create Tag Only for an existing standalone tag is rejected on the shared New Release form with a release-exists error.
bugs.expected: After the first Create Tag Only action, the standalone tag should exist without a release. Retrying with that existing tag may be rejected as a duplicate tag, but should not claim a release exists when the tag-only flow did not create one.
bugs.actual: The first Create Tag Only submission creates the tag and opens its Code page. Retrying the same action for that existing tag displays “A release with this tag name already exists.” The duplicate is rejected; no publishing failure or data loss was established.
reproSteps: Sign in as eval and open Releases > New Release in the seeded eval/harbor-handbook repository.
Enter a fresh unique tag name, keep main as the target, and leave release title and body blank.
Click Create Tag Only and confirm the tag-created message and the tag Code page.
Return through Releases > New Release, enter the same tag and confirm the Existing tag helper.
Click Create Tag Only again and observe the release-exists validation error on the form.
bugs.reason: User-approved rejection of the wording-only complaint. The existing tag is correctly rejected as a duplicate in the shared New Release form. The user does not consider the shared release-exists wording an actionable bug for this eval; no functional failure is established.

bugs.name: Release-notes Preview does not render Bold toolbar text in bold
bugs.summary: The release-notes Bold toolbar inserts `**Bold phrase**`, but Preview renders the phrase in regular weight after loading.
bugs.expected: Text formatted with the Bold toolbar should appear visibly bold in the release-notes Preview.
bugs.actual: The Write view visibly contained `# Lifecycle Deep Bold Preview` and `**Bold phrase**`; Preview rendered the heading as a heading but displayed “Bold phrase” in regular weight, still unchanged after six seconds.
reproSteps: Sign in as eval and open New Release in eval/harbor-handbook without publishing a release.
Compare the earlier and later Preview attempts in the original recording: the earlier editor value is plain Bold phrase, with no Markdown emphasis markers.
After the retry, the editor value contains a Markdown heading followed by **Bold phrase**. Open Preview and inspect the correctly formatted phrase.
Keep the distinction between the two inputs: plain text should preview as plain text, while the corrected Markdown should preview as bold.
bugs.reason: User-approved rejection after reviewing the earlier and later Preview states. The earlier attempt replaced the toolbar’s Markdown markers and submitted plain text. The corrected retry preserved **Bold phrase**, rendered a strong element at semibold weight, and the user confirmed that the later Preview visibly showed bold. The observed change follows the changed input; no Preview failure is established.

bugs.name: Deleting a release leaves its title and notes visible on the tag page
bugs.summary: The report says that after Delete Release (keeping the tag), the release's title and notes still appear on the tag's page at /releases/tag/<tag>.
bugs.expected: The reported expectation is that deleting a release removes its title and notes from the tag's page while keeping the Git tag.
bugs.actual: After deleting a published release on a tag without its own message, /releases/tag/<tag> still showed the release title and notes. The release was gone from the Releases list.
reproSteps: Publish a release on a tag without ticking the tag-message option.
Delete the release with Delete Release (not Delete Tag).
Open the tag's page.
bugs.reason: Delete Release (keeping the tag) only marks the release row as a tag (services/release/release.go), so its title and notes stay attached to the surviving tag. The user judged keeping that text on the tag acceptable, consistent with tags showing their message, rather than a defect. The tag page, the tags RSS/Atom feed and the New Release prefill are separate rejections of this same behavior, so each report is matched once per run.

bugs.name: Release-notes Preview keeps showing stale content after Bold formatting
bugs.summary: The report claims that after formatting release notes with the Bold toolbar button and switching to Preview, the Preview pane doesn't update and keeps showing the previous content instead of the bold text.
bugs.expected: The reporter expects Preview to show the newly entered notes in bold.
bugs.actual: After entering 'Responsive toolbar note', selecting it, clicking Bold and then Preview at 768×900, the Preview pane was reported to still show the earlier preview.
reproSteps: Open a New Release form at 768×900.
Enter text in the notes, select it and click the Bold toolbar button.
Click Preview.
bugs.reason: Not reproduced. Preview sends the current notes on every click and replaces the pane with the server's response (web_src/js/features/comp/ComboMarkdownEditor.ts), which rendered the text as <strong> each time. The previous preview stays visible only until that response arrives (about 50–100 ms), a loading state rather than stale content. Bold rendering itself is already rejected as gitea-pass2-014.

bugs.name: Deleting a release leaves its notes in the tags RSS/Atom feed
bugs.summary: The report says that after Delete Release (keeping the tag), the tags RSS or Atom feed still shows the deleted release's notes for that tag.
bugs.expected: The reporter expects the deleted release's notes to disappear from the tags feed.
bugs.actual: After deleting a published release and keeping its tag, tags.rss and tags.atom showed the tag with the release's notes (the item title becomes the tag name).
reproSteps: Publish a release with notes on a new tag.
Delete the release, keeping the tag.
Open the repository's tags.rss or tags.atom feed and find the tag.
bugs.reason: Delete Release (keeping the tag) only marks the release row as a tag (services/release/release.go), so its title and notes stay attached to the surviving tag. The user judged keeping that text on the tag acceptable, consistent with tags showing their message, rather than a defect. The tags feed renders each tag row's notes (routers/web/feed/convert.go). The tag page, the tags RSS/Atom feed and the New Release prefill are separate rejections of this same behavior, so each report is matched once per run.

bugs.name: Deleting a release leaves its title and notes pre-filled in New Release for the tag
bugs.summary: The report says that after Delete Release (keeping the tag), starting a New Release for that tag pre-fills the deleted release's title and notes.
bugs.expected: The reporter expects New Release for the tag to start empty.
bugs.actual: After deleting a published release and keeping its tag, New Release from the tag pre-filled the old title and notes.
reproSteps: Publish a release with a title and notes on a new tag.
Delete the release, keeping the tag.
Start a New Release for that tag and look at the title and notes fields.
bugs.reason: Delete Release (keeping the tag) only marks the release row as a tag (services/release/release.go), so its title and notes stay attached to the surviving tag. The user judged keeping that text on the tag acceptable, consistent with tags showing their message, rather than a defect. New Release for an existing tag pre-fills from that tag row. The tag page, the tags RSS/Atom feed and the New Release prefill are separate rejections of this same behavior, so each report is matched once per run.

bugs.name: Root-relative release-note images resolve under the repository path and appear broken
bugs.summary: The report says that a Markdown image in release notes written with a leading slash, such as /avatars/<hash>, is rewritten under the repository path and shows as a broken image in Preview and on the saved release, while the same image as a full URL loads.
bugs.expected: The reported expectation is that a leading-slash image path resolves from the site root.
bugs.actual: The image src became /<owner>/<repo>/avatars/<hash>, which 404s, so only the alt text and broken-image icon appeared.
reproSteps: Open New Release in a repository.
Enter notes containing ![avatar](/avatars/<hash>?size=48) and the same image as a full URL.
Click Preview, then Save Draft, and compare the two images.
bugs.reason: Intended: since Gitea 1.23 (go-gitea/gitea#34114), a leading-slash Markdown path is relative to the current render context, not the site root, so content stays portable when cloned, mirrored or served under a sub-path; /:root/... links to the site root. Release notes are rendered with renderhelper.NewRenderContextRepoComment (routers/web/repo/release.go), whose ResolveLink sends non-root links through ResolveLinkRelative with the repository link, and models/renderhelper/repo_comment_test.go asserts ![/image](/image) renders as /user2/repo1/image. Same rule as the known-invalid 'Root-relative links in issue Markdown are prefixed with the repository path' and the wiki root-relative image and link entries.

bugs.name: Selecting more than five release attachments silently drops the extra files
bugs.summary: The report says selecting six files in the New Release uploader attaches only the first five and silently drops the sixth.
bugs.expected: The reported expectation is that every selected file is attached, or that the user is told why one was not.
bugs.actual: Selecting six files at once attached five and showed a persistent red toast, 'Dropzone upload error: You can not upload any more files.' Publishing created the release with five assets.
reproSteps: Open New Release in a repository.
Select six files at once in the attachment dropzone.
Check how many files attach and whether an error is shown.
bugs.reason: Not reproducible as reported / intended limit: the fixture uses Gitea's default [attachment] MAX_FILES=5 (modules/setting/attachment.go), passed to the dropzone as data-max-file. Dropzone rejects the sixth file and web_src/js/features/dropzone.ts shows a persistent error toast and removes its preview, so the file is not silently dropped.

bugs.name: External release asset is shown as a 0 B file and its link serves an empty file instead of going to the external URL
bugs.summary: The report says posting external_url=https://example.com/doc.pdf to the release-assets API creates a 0 B attachment served from /attachments/<uuid> instead of a link to the external URL.
bugs.expected: The reported expectation is that the asset links to the external URL.
bugs.actual: A form-urlencoded POST of external_url to .../releases/<id>/assets?name=extdoc.pdf returned 201 with size 0. The release page listed 'extdoc.pdf 0 B' and its link served an empty file.
reproSteps: Open the release-assets endpoint in the instance's API docs and note its accepted parameters.
POST external_url=https://example.com/doc.pdf as a form-urlencoded body to /api/v1/repos/<owner>/<repo>/releases/<id>/assets?name=extdoc.pdf.
Open the release page and the asset link.
bugs.reason: Unsupported feature: Gitea 1.24.7 has no external (link) release assets; external_url is a Forgejo API field. Gitea's API docs list only a multipart 'attachment' or an octet-stream body, and the New/Edit Release UI offers only file uploads. routers/api/v1/repo/release_attachment.go treats a non-multipart body as the file content, so the empty body that was sent was stored as received.
